correctness.rationale: The equation is 2Q^3+P^2 with Q=X²+Y²+Z² and P=XYZ. The gradient forces either a single zero coordinate with Q=0 or three equal nonzero squared coordinates. The finite singular support also excludes a repeated component. At the six axis points, P,Q are parameters, giving A2 and one rational branch; the four remaining points have tangent discriminant 3 and two conjugate branches. Every component has degree divisible by three by intersecting an axis (the only intersections are transverse axis–conic supports with curve–axis multiplicity three); two cubic components would each have three cusps, impossible. The genus defect is ten, and the normalization has a rational point. Normalization-unit quotients give one additive group per cusp and one torus per node; the morphism to the norm-one torus is a↦a/σ(a), with σ the nontrivial field automorphism on the coefficient algebra, not absolute Frobenius on variable points. The normalization fibers give correction −4(−1)^m and zeta numerator (1+U)^4. Independent symbolic and finite checks in /workspace/review_replay.py reproduce the mod-5 equation, the tangent discriminants and counts 10,22 over F5,F25. The geometric arguments, not the two counts, prove the extension formulas.
